gloss: pleasure quarter; red-light district (historical); enclosure; compound; bailey (of a castle)

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}の{廓|くるわ}は{独特|どくとく}の{文化|ぶんか}を{持|も}っていた。
examples.english: The pleasure quarters of the Edo period had a unique culture.

examples.japanese: {吉原|よしわら}は{江戸|えど}で{最|もっと}も{有名|ゆうめい}な{廓|くるわ}だった。
examples.english: Yoshiwara was the most famous pleasure quarter in Edo.

examples.japanese: {廓|くるわ}の{中|なか}では{独自|どくじ}の{言葉遣|ことばづか}いや{風習|ふうしゅう}があり、{多|おお}くの{文学|ぶんがく}{作品|さくひん}の{舞台|ぶたい}になった。
examples.english: The pleasure quarters had their own distinctive speech and customs, and became the setting for many literary works.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}の{廓|くるわ}を{見学|けんがく}する。
{本丸|ほんまる}の{廓|くるわ}は{石垣|いしがき}で{囲|かこ}まれている。
examples.english: The main keep's compound is surrounded by stone walls.

examples.japanese: この{城跡|しろあと}には{三|みっ}つの{廓|くるわ}が{残|のこ}っており、{当時|とうじ}の{規模|きぼ}がうかがえる。
examples.english: Three baileys remain at this castle ruin, giving a sense of its former scale.

notes:
Also written as {郭|くるわ}. Has two distinct historical meanings that share the concept of an enclosed, walled-off area.

PLEASURE QUARTER USAGE:
Refers to the walled entertainment districts of the Edo period (1603-1868) where licensed prostitution operated. The most famous was {吉原|よしわら} in Edo (modern Tokyo). These districts developed rich cultural traditions including distinctive speech patterns ({廓|くるわ}{言葉|ことば}), fashion, music, and art that influenced Japanese literature and kabuki theater.

CASTLE USAGE:
In castle architecture, {廓|くるわ} (or {曲輪|くるわ}) refers to the enclosed areas within a castle's defensive walls. Castles typically had multiple {廓|くるわ}: the {本丸|ほんまる} (main compound), {二|に}の{丸|まる} (second compound), and {三|さん}の{丸|まる} (third compound).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {遊郭|ゆうかく}: pleasure quarter — a more common reading/writing, specifically for the entertainment district sense
- {花街|かがい}: geisha quarter — a district of teahouses and geisha entertainment, distinct from {廓|くるわ}
- {曲輪|くるわ}: bailey, compound — the castle-specific spelling
